precepts.text: My heart is not haughty; I have behaved and quieted myself as a child that is weaned of his mother.
precepts.point: Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Stay humble with it. “Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me. Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.”

David behaved and quieted himself as a weaned child. Desiring the milk of the word instead of running to things too high for you is that same humble spirit.

precepts.text: Seek not the things too hard for thee; think on what is commanded with reverence, not curious in unnecessary matters.
precepts.point: Many babes fall because instead of consuming the milk they try to go straight for the meat. The teaching is about brothers and sisters who reach for things a little too hard.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why:
David says his heart is not haughty nor his eyes lofty; he does not think he is better than anyone and is not proud above measure, and he does not exercise himself in great matters or in things too high for him. “Seek not out things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret. Be not curious in unnecessary matters: for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand.”

Many babes fall because instead of consuming the milk they try to go straight for the meat. Brothers and sisters reach for things a little too hard, when what is commanded is to be thought upon with reverence.

precepts.text: As newborn babes desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow thereby.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why: “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. David behaves and quiets himself, calming himself as a child weaned of his mother. Coming into the truth we must desire the sincere milk of the word, the basics, and grow from there.

precepts.text: You have need to be taught again the first principles; he that uses milk is unskillful, for he is a babe.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why:
“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat. For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” Some have need to be taught again the first principles; he that uses milk is unskillful in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe.

That is why we come back to this Bible as a child, quieting ourselves like a weaned child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older, because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

precepts.text: Except you be converted and become as little children you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why: “Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.” We have to come back to this Bible as a child, the way David quieted himself as a child weaned of his mother. Age is a carnal thing; what counts is being converted and becoming as a little child that desires the milk of the word.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.
precepts.point: Our hope lies in this Bible. We get hope through the patience and comfort of the scriptures, because we have been taught wrong all our lives and must be converted back as a child.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why:
“Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.” The only people who have hope in the Most High are the Israelites, the so-called blacks, Spanish, and native Indians today. Our hope lies in this Bible: “whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We have been taught wrong all our lives and must be converted back as a child, and the patience and comfort of the scriptures is where that hope comes from.

precepts.text: King David quiets himself as a weaned child and says, "Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever."
precepts.point: "O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee" is again the cry of patience. As Passover approaches spirits can get shaky, so the word is brought to heal you and remind you that when you go through trials your faith is being tested, the way Ecclesiasticus 2 must be applied.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.” It is again the cry of patience, and King David shows how to carry it: “Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me. Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child. Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.”

King David quiets himself as a weaned child, not haughty, not reaching into things too high for him, and says, “Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and for ever.” As Passover approaches spirits can get shaky, so the word is brought to heal you and remind you that when you go through trials your faith is being tested, the way Ecclesiasticus 2 must be applied. Quiet yourself, wait for him, and hope in the Lord; he is our salvation in the time of trouble.
